judged_text: Dead/broken fallback in Google CalendarService updateEvent (~254-256) and deleteEvent (~314-317): `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — the find() branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, then searches for cal.externalId === undefined/null which can never match, so the old destinationCalendar.externalId fallback is effectively deleted and calendarId is passed as undefined to the Google API; bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (pre-refactor bookings, and new bookings via the no-credentialId path) now fail to update/delete their Google event.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar as:

```ts
externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId
```

But the `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null/""), and then it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null/""`), which will typically never match a real calendar externalId. This effectively removes the previous fallback to the event’s destination calendar and can cause update/delete to target the wrong calendar (or rely on later defaults like `primary`), breaking updates/deletes for bookings whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId`.
